description: Start tracking a container, bill of lading or booking number. Type and carrier are detected when omitted; if the carrier is not recognised the shipment is added but not tracked, and you should call again with `carrier` (SCAC, see list_carriers). Already tracked references are returned as they are (archived ones are re-activated), so repeating a call is safe. Required: reference (4-64 characters, e.g. MSCU1234566). Optional: ref_type (container, bl, booking), carrier, customer_reference, tags, booking_number and bl_number (the other numbers of the same shipment, e.g. a container with its booking: one shipment, not three). Returns: result (created or exists), shipment {id, reference, ref_type, carrier, customer_reference, status, tracking_status, phase, pol, pod, eta, original_eta, delay_hours, predicted_eta, eta_risk, vessel, containers, booking_number, bl_number, tracked_via}. The first carrier data arrives in the background: check get_shipment a minute later. Counts towards the plan's monthly allowance once the carrier returns data. Needs write access: a read + write API key, or read + write access granted at sign-in by an owner or admin of the company.

bl_number.description: Bill of lading number of the same shipment, e.g. with a container reference.

booking_number.description: Booking number of the same shipment, e.g. with a container reference.

carrier.description: Carrier SCAC. Auto-detected when omitted; required when detection fails (see list_carriers).

company.description: Which company to act for: its id, @handle or exact name (see list_companies). Omit for the connection's default company.

reference.description: Container (ISO 6346, e.g. MSCU1234566), bill of lading or booking number.

name: track_shipment
title: Track shipment
